guidance.checkinTodo: Send a reminder: without their ID documents, the declaration cannot be filed in time.

guidance.invitationTodo: Send a new invitation, or withdraw it if it is no longer needed.

guidance.einvoiceTodo: Correct the invoice and resubmit it: as it stands the legal obligation is unmet.

guidance.automationTodo: Check the rule, and do it by hand if a guest is affected.

guidance.integrationTodo: Reconnect the integration: while it is silent, availability no longer flows back.

actionCard.failed: The action failed. This item still needs handling.
actionCard.elsewhere: This is not done from here — the line will disappear once the cause is dealt with.
actionCard.noiseWhat: A noise threshold was exceeded at the property.
actionCard.noiseConsequence: Left alone, this is what precedes a neighbour complaint — and a fine in some cities.
actionCard.payoutWhat: A payout is prepared but nobody approved it.
actionCard.payoutConsequence: The owner is waiting for their transfer, and nothing goes out while the decision is missing.
actionCard.approved: Payout approved — it will go out on the next run.
actionCard.depositWhat: The deposit is still held several days after checkout.
actionCard.depositConsequence: The guest's money stays blocked on their card: a complaint is coming, then a review.
actionCard.released: Deposit released with the payment provider.
actionCard.invitationConsequence: The person can no longer join the organisation, and nothing tells them so.
actionCard.invitationResent: New invitation sent, with a fresh deadline.
actionCard.issueWhat: A report from the field is awaiting a decision.
actionCard.issueConsequence: While it stays open, the damage is neither repaired nor dismissed — simply forgotten.
actionCard.outboxWhat: An internal message exhausted every retry.
actionCard.outboxConsequence: Its consequences show up elsewhere — a calendar never informed, so a possible double booking.
actionCard.replayed: Message queued again — it will go out within seconds.
actionCard.reservationWhat: This booking was never confirmed and the arrival is close.
actionCard.reservationConsequence: While pending, it is excluded from everything else: no cleaning, no stay message, no balance claimed.
actionCard.interventionUnassignedConsequence: On the day, nobody will turn up — and the guest will be the one to tell you.
actionCard.interventionUnpaidConsequence: The provider is waiting to be paid, and the job will not close on its own.
actionCard.checkinConsequence: Without their ID documents, the guest declaration cannot be filed in time.
actionCard.onboardingConsequence: Everything looks configured, and yet no payout will ever go out.
actionCard.einvoiceConsequence: The legal obligation is unmet, while the client already holds the invoice.
actionCard.automationConsequence: The product shows the rule as active, and the guest received nothing.
actionCard.integrationConsequence: While it is silent, availability no longer flows back — the leading cause of double bookings.
actionCard.confirmed: Booking confirmed and dates blocked on the calendar.
actionCard.automationReplayed: Rule replayed — check that it went through this time.
actionCard.conflict: These dates are already taken: confirming would create a double booking.
actionCard.interventionOverdueWhat: This job's date has passed and it is still not finished.
actionCard.interventionOverdueConsequence: The property may not be ready for the next arrival, and nobody said why.
actionCard.declarationWhat: The stay happened without the guest form (police form, DGSN depending on the property's country) being filled in.
actionCard.declarationConsequence: Only the guest can fill it, from their welcome guide: once the stay is over, nobody can file it on their behalf.
actionCard.conversationWhat: The last message in this conversation came from the guest.
actionCard.conversationConsequence: Silence during a stay is paid for in reviews — it is the most frequent complaint in bad ratings.
actionCard.guideWhat: No welcome guide published for this property, and an arrival is close.
actionCard.guideConsequence: The guest will receive a dead link, and the access code cannot be delivered to them.

explain.default: This event was recorded by the platform.
explain.reservation: A stay changed: creation, update, cancellation or guest access. Tasks already scheduled on the former dates do not move on their own.
explain.payment: Money moved, or failed to move. The payment provider is the source of truth: the amount shown here is the one it confirmed.
explain.intervention: A field intervention changed state. The full detail — photos, notes, assignee, duration — stays on its record.
explain.service_request: A request is waiting for a decision: approval, rejection, assignment to a team, or conversion into an intervention.
explain.document: A document was produced, sent or signed. The file itself lives in the document history.
explain.contact: A message came through the internal inbox or the public contact form.
explain.guest_messaging: An exchange with a guest happened, or could not go through. On failure, the guest received nothing.
explain.team: A team’s composition or permissions changed.
explain.system: Platform event: channel sync, configuration, integration or user account.
explain.SUPERVISION_SUGGESTION: An agent spotted something on a property and is proposing a move — it does not act alone. The card is waiting for your approval in that property's supervision queue.
explain.SUPERVISION_AUTO_APPLIED: An agent applied a move you had authorised as automatic. This is a report: nothing is waiting on you.
explain.SUPERVISION_AUTO_RULE_SUGGESTED: The same move comes back often enough to deserve a rule: the agent offers to automate it rather than ask you again.
explain.ACCESS_CODE_ROTATED: The guest's departure triggered the renewal of this property's access code. The code shown here is the one IN FORCE, read just now: a more recent rotation would have made the one in the message stale.
explain.SMART_LOCK_CODE_ROTATED_MANUALLY: Someone manually regenerated this lock's code — the panel names who did it. The previous code no longer works, including for anyone it had been shared with.
explain.SMART_LOCK_CODE_ROTATED_MANUALLY_actor: {{actor}} manually regenerated this lock's code. The previous code no longer works, including for anyone it had been shared with.
explain.SMART_LOCK_CODE_GENERATION_FAILED: The lock rejected the code: none was set. The guest will arrive at a door that will not open.
explain.SMART_LOCK_CODE_DELIVERY_FAILED: The code is on the lock, but the guest never received it. This is not a missed message: it is an arrival that will fail.
explain.PAYMENT_CONFIRMED: Payment for this job has arrived. The file above is the one that was just paid — it is recalled here so you can check the amount against what was ordered.

nextStep.default: Open the related screen to act on the item behind this notification.
nextStep.reservation: Open the reservation to check dates, payment and the interventions already scheduled.
nextStep.payment: Match the amount against the related invoice, then chase or refund from Billing.
nextStep.intervention: Open the record to follow progress, validate the work or chase the assignee.
nextStep.service_request: Handle the request: approve, reject, or assign it to an available team.
nextStep.document: Check the generated document and, if needed, send it again to its recipient.
nextStep.contact: Reply from the inbox so the exchange stays attached to the contact.
nextStep.guest_messaging: Confirm the guest actually received the message; otherwise fix their details and send again.
nextStep.team: Review the team’s access if the change did not come from you.
nextStep.system: Nothing to do while everything is green. Otherwise, open the related screen to retry.
nextStep.SUPERVISION_SUGGESTION: Open the card in the supervision queue: it restates the exact situation at the moment of acting, and the move runs from there in one click.
nextStep.SUPERVISION_AUTO_APPLIED: Nothing to do. If the move does not suit you, the automation rule is tuned in Automations.
nextStep.SUPERVISION_AUTO_RULE_SUGGESTED: Decide whether this move should become automatic — otherwise the agent keeps proposing it card by card.
nextStep.ACCESS_CODE_ROTATED: Carry the code over to the keybox: it is the one place the platform does not update by itself.
nextStep.SMART_LOCK_CODE_ROTATED_MANUALLY: Open the lock under Connected objects to read the new code. If a stay is in progress, the guest has already received it by message.
nextStep.SMART_LOCK_CODE_GENERATION_FAILED: Open the lock under Connected objects: its history gives the exact reason, and Generate retries once the cause is fixed.
nextStep.SMART_LOCK_CODE_DELIVERY_FAILED: Check that an Access code or Check-in message template is active, then send the code to the guest right away.
nextStep.PAYMENT_CONFIRMED: Nothing to do: the payment is recorded. Open the file if the amount does not match what was ordered.

s0.highlight: {{agentCount}} AI agents watch over every side of your business
s0.subtitle: Pricing, guest messaging, housekeeping, payments, reviews, calendars, compliance, owner relations, distribution: each holds its own trade, all of them in step. The only thing left in your hands: the strategy.

s1.highlight: you keep the final say on every action
s1.subtitle: Your agents set prices, answer guests, write your briefings and flag anomalies. Every sensitive action waits for your approval, and the ones you delegate stay in the log.

s2.subtitle: Multilingual messaging that answers arrival questions, Wi-Fi codes and local recommendations — over WhatsApp and email alike, in a single thread. You handle the exceptions, the AI handles the routine.

s4.highlight: with their calendar and their bookings
s4.subtitle: Import from your existing channels, over iCal or a direct connection. Your current stays are carried over, not retyped. Listing descriptions are AI-generated, then reworked by you.

s5.highlight: every one of your distribution channels
s5.subtitle: One calendar is the source of truth: after every change, availability goes back out to each channel. Gaps and double bookings are detected and surfaced — not discovered by the guest.

s6.tagline: Access codes generated on the fly.
s6.subtitle: The code expires automatically at check-out, the lock battery is monitored, keys left at a key-box are tracked in real time. You never hand out a code manually again.

s8.highlight: in France, Morocco and Saudi Arabia
s8.subtitle: Each country has its own tax profile, currency and invoice numbering. Filings prepared, supplier invoices imported, and your revenue consolidated on a single dashboard.

s9.subtitle: Management mandates, short-term rental contracts, arrival authorisations. Built-in electronic signature backed by a timestamped certificate, with no third-party tool to pay for alongside.

s11.subtitle: A booking site you compose without writing a line of code, wired to your calendar, your prices and your payments. What you sell direct, you keep.

s12.subtitle: Wi-Fi, arrival, house rules, the good addresses nearby: a web page that opens from a link, with no app to install. You build it once, it follows every stay.

s13.subtitle: Operations, technical and regulatory, guest services, owner services: you find the provider, you request a quote and you follow the job without leaving Baitly.

s14.subtitle: Your add-ons appear at booking time and in the welcome guide, are paid online and land in your statements. Nothing to chase by hand.

s15.tagline: A party at your place at midnight:
s15.highlight: you hear about it before the neighbour does
s15.subtitle: Sensors measure the sound level against the threshold you set. Above it, the guest gets a reminder and you get the alert, with the level and the time slot. Decibels, never a recording.

s16.subtitle: Comparables in your city, booking pace, price positioning. The Revenue agent proposes an adjustment, and never steps outside the floor and ceiling you set for each property.

teardown.onboardingChecklist: Master-detail getting-started guide: groups on the left, steps as an accordion on the right. Three step states (done, to do, locked by plan), duration estimate, a Skip action, and two progress granularities shown together.
teardown.showcaseEmpty: Two-column showcase empty state for screens that are empty before setup: the title carries the value proposition, the right column previews the filled product, and the fallback avoids a dead end when the main action assumes a missing prerequisite.
teardown.settingSentence: A setting written as a sentence with inline controls (“Mark the property [unknown] after [5] days”) — the rule reads as a rule instead of being rebuilt from a stack of fields.
teardown.optionalSection: Optional section block inside a long form: tinted panel, “(optional)” mention, fields revealed only on demand — required fields keep the visual weight.
teardown.channelBadges: Channel badge cluster with connection state (validation pastille, disconnected channels desaturated but still readable), with an overlay variant for property photos.
teardown.cornerRibbon: Diagonal corner ribbon (promo, exclusive, new) — flags an offer on a card without taking space in the content flow. The parent must be positioned and clip overflow.
teardown.onboardingDock: Floating, persistent getting-started dock: the guide follows the user from screen to screen instead of living only on the home page. Three states (collapsed, expanded, completed), group navigation via a pager, global progress visible in every state, and always dismissible.

help.title: How does the Outbox work?
help.description: Every business mutation (booking, user profile, calendar…) writes an event into the outbox table in the SAME transaction as the data. The Kafka relay then reads those events and publishes them to the matching topic. Guarantee: at-least-once, no loss.

pending.title: PENDING — waiting
pending.description: The event is queued. The Kafka relay will pick it up on the next cycle (a few seconds).

sent.title: SENT — published
sent.description: The event has been published to Kafka. Downstream consumers can now process it.

failed.title: FAILED — needs investigation
failed.description: Publishing failed (missing topic, broker unavailable, invalid payload). Check the Error column, fix the cause, then click “Retry Selected” to requeue the event.

pending.title: Queued
pending.what: The event is stored in the database; the Kafka relay will pick it up on the next cycle (a few seconds).
pending.todo: No action needed — the move to SENT or FAILED is automatic.

sent.title: Sent
sent.what: The event was published to the Kafka topic. Downstream consumers can now process it.

failed.title: Failed
failed.what: Publishing to Kafka failed (missing topic, broker unavailable, invalid payload). The ERROR column has the detail.
failed.todo: Fix the underlying cause, then click “Retry Selected” to requeue the event.

columns.id: Internal id of the event in the outbox table.

columns.topic: Target Kafka topic. If a topic does not exist on the broker, sends end up FAILED.
columns.status: PENDING = queued, SENT = published, FAILED = error. Hover the chip for the detail and the recommended action.
columns.retry: Number of attempts already made. Incremented on each relay failure.
columns.error: Error message from the last attempt. Hover the row to see the full message.
columns.createdAt: When the event was stored in the outbox (= when the business mutation happened).
columns.sentAt: When the event was successfully published to Kafka. Empty until it is SENT.

YOUSIGN.description: Certified French trust service provider. SES, AES and QES electronic signatures (legally equivalent to a handwritten one). The integration is implemented in Baitly: enter your API key, then switch the signature provider to enable it.
YOUSIGN.access: A Yousign account is required (free 40-day sandbox). Generate the API key under Settings → API. Priced per signature volume (roughly €0.50–€2 per signature depending on the plan).

DOCUSEAL.description: A self-hosted open-source alternative: SES signature with cryptographic PDF sealing, data on your own infrastructure, no licence fee. The integration is implemented in Baitly; it needs the instance deployed, then the provider switched.
DOCUSEAL.access: Self-hosted: a Docker container in your infrastructure, plus the base URL and API key variables. Free (AGPL licence).

PENNYLANE.description: A French accounting solution with built-in electronic signature. Used by more than 250,000 small businesses in France. OAuth2 connection to the business API.
PENNYLANE.access: A Pennylane developer account (by application). Client ID and secret after approval. The API is free for accounting invoice sync.

AIRBTICS.description: Target market-data provider: benchmarks for average rate, occupancy and revenue by area, deep Morocco coverage (Marrakech, Casablanca, Agadir since 2019), native output in dirhams.
AIRBTICS.access: An Airbtics subscription (roughly $500–$2,000 a year). Enter the API key here: it enables the daily ingestion at the next cycle, with no redeployment.

AIRROI.description: Pay-per-call market-data top-up (about $0.01 a call, no contract): a precision cross-check against your own data, and coverage where other sources are thin.
AIRROI.access: An AirROI account (pay as you go). Enter the API key here: 5 markets refreshed daily costs about $18 a year.

QUICKBOOKS.description: The world's leading accounting solution. Widely used in the US, UK, Canada and Australia. Syncs invoices, expenses and consolidated financial reporting.
QUICKBOOKS.access: An Intuit developer account (free sandbox). Create an app to get the client ID and secret. OAuth2 with a realm ID for multi-company setups.

XERO.description: Leading cloud accounting in the UK, Australia and New Zealand. Growing fast in the US and Europe. Multi-tenant: one account can manage several accounting organisations.
XERO.access: A free Xero developer account. Create an app to get the client ID and secret. OAuth2 with the offline access scope for refresh tokens.

SAGE.description: Sage Business Cloud Accounting, the leading small-business accounting suite in France and Europe. Several companies under one account.
SAGE.access: A Sage developer account plus a partner agreement. Client ID and secret after approval (about two weeks). OAuth2 with full access.

CHEKIN.description: A Spanish service that automates the police record and its European equivalents. Guest identity checks, certificate generation and automatic filing with the authorities.
CHEKIN.access: A Chekin Pro account (about €5 per check-in depending on the plan). API key under Settings → Integrations once subscribed.

POLICE_MA.description: A direct connector to Morocco's national security directorate. Guest declaration is mandatory from the first night, with regular checks on establishments.
POLICE_MA.access: An establishment account with the DGSN (registered through the official portal or the local prefecture). Establishment ID and API key are issued to declared hosts.

ABSHER_KSA.description: Absher, the Saudi Ministry of Interior's national platform. Registration of non-resident guests is mandatory, tied into tourism checks.
ABSHER_KSA.access: Register the establishment through the ministry portal. The API key is issued after administrative approval and a tourism licence.

SHOMOOS.description: Shomoos (شموس), the Saudi national guest-registration platform for accommodation. It is the sector's official channel, with registration mandatory on arrival.
SHOMOOS.access: A Shomoos establishment subscription (an accommodation licence is required). API access is limited to registered establishments and approved integrators.

SUMSUB.description: A leader in identity verification across the Middle East and Europe. Individual and business verification plus transaction monitoring. Accepted by Saudi banks and European payment bodies.
SUMSUB.access: A Sumsub account (roughly €0.50–€3 per verification depending on the plan). App token and API key in the dashboard, developers section.

VERIFF.description: Estonian identity verification known for its value for money. Liveness detection, document checks and anti-money-laundering screening. European, Middle East and global coverage.
VERIFF.access: A Veriff account (free trial, then volume pricing, about €1–€2 per verification). API key under Settings → Integrations.

ONFIDO.description: Premium identity verification (UK). Outstanding user experience, embedded in major fintechs. Around a 95% approval rate and AI fraud detection.
ONFIDO.access: An Onfido account (volume pricing, pricier but higher quality). API key in the dashboard, tokens section.

SITEMINDER.description: A world-leading channel manager (Australia). Around 250 platforms integrated, including niche markets in the Middle East, Asia and Latin America. Widely used by independent hotels and premium management agencies.
SITEMINDER.access: A SiteMinder partner agreement (from about $80 per property per month). The API key is issued after commercial onboarding.

HOSTAWAY.description: A short-stay channel manager (US). Native integration with the main platforms. A direct competitor of the sector's large PMS players.
HOSTAWAY.access: A Hostaway account (roughly $30–$50 per property per month). API key under Settings → API, with an IP allowlist.

RENTALS_UNITED.description: A short-stay channel manager (Spain). More than 60 platforms, including the Middle East and Central Europe. Widely used in France and Morocco by multi-property agencies.
RENTALS_UNITED.access: A Rentals United account (about €30 per property per month). API credentials under Settings → Integration.

CHANNEX.description: A short-stay channel manager (UK). More than 100 platforms, a modern REST API with webhooks and full public documentation. Recommended for agencies managing 10 to 50 properties.
CHANNEX.access: A pay-as-you-go Channex account (about £10, £8 or £6 per property per month depending on tier). Free sandbox. API key in the dashboard after onboarding, which takes under a day.

airbnb.description: The world leader in short-term rentals. Native OAuth2 connection through the partner API. Around 70% of French short-stay bookings.
airbnb.access: An Airbnb partner account (by application). Client ID and secret after approval. Scopes: listings, bookings, messaging.

booking.description: The leading hotel and rental platform. Very strong in Europe, growing in the Middle East. Connected through its connectivity service, with a property ID.
booking.access: A pro extranet account plus a connectivity access request (two to four weeks of review). Credentials are provided by the account manager.

expedia.description: A leading platform in the US and the head of the Expedia group. Connected through the group's partner solution, with a key and secret.
expedia.access: A partner portal account and access to the solution by application. Key and secret once contracted.

hotels.description: An Expedia group subsidiary focused on the US and European markets. Shares Expedia's technical interface, adding visibility across its network.
hotels.access: Included in the Expedia partner agreement. Properties are enabled one by one from the portal.

agoda.description: An Asian platform focused on Asia and the Middle East. Heavily used by Saudi and Emirati travellers. Connected through its yield control system.
agoda.access: A partner hub account plus API activation on request. Property ID and key provided by the account manager.

tripcom.description: A Chinese platform that opens the Chinese and Asian traveller markets. Growing fast in the Middle East. Connectivity through its open distribution platform.
tripcom.access: A partner account and platform access by application. Partner ID and key issued after commercial approval.

vrbo.description: An Expedia subsidiary specialised in short-term rentals. A direct Airbnb competitor on houses and villas.
vrbo.access: A partner central account. OAuth2 and a listing ID. API access through the group portal.

abritel.description: The French brand of the Vrbo and Expedia group, focused on holiday rentals in France. Shares Vrbo's technical infrastructure.
abritel.access: Included in the Vrbo partner agreement. Listing ID and OAuth tokens.

hometogo.description: A German metasearch engine aggregating more than 25 million listings. Multi-platform distribution and an iCal connection for individual properties.
hometogo.access: A partner account, a partner ID and your system's iCal feed URL. Properties are validated manually.

gathern.description: A Saudi platform specialising in chalet and villa rentals. Heavily used locally for weekends and domestic tourism.
gathern.access: A Gathern partner account (local approval and a tourism licence are required). The API key is issued after onboarding.

rentelly.description: A business-to-business platform for short-stay rental brokerage in the Middle East. Connects hosts to local wholesale distributors.
rentelly.access: A Rentelly partner account. The API key is issued after a commercial agreement.

kease.description: A Middle East business-to-business platform for multi-platform distribution of short-stay rentals. Focused on the Saudi and Emirati markets.
kease.access: A Kease partner account. An API key and commercial onboarding are required.

stay.description: The official Saudi tourism platform. A programme dedicated to licensed accommodation.
stay.access: A licensed establishment is required (identity checks and tourism classification). The API key is issued by the authority.

mabeet.description: A Saudi booking platform for both businesses and the public. Focused on domestic tourism and religious travellers.
mabeet.access: A Mabeet partner account. The API key is issued after a commercial agreement and tourism licence approval.

almosafer.description: Saudi Arabia's leading platform, around 6 million monthly active users. A real differentiator for the Saudi market: no Western system integrates it natively.
almosafer.access: A partner agreement with the group is required (a long commercial review). API key and endpoints are provided once agreed.

tajawal.description: A Middle East platform from the same group as Almosafer. Number one for short stays in the region, with a strong presence in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt.
tajawal.access: Included in the group agreement. Properties are enabled case by case.

wego.description: The dominant metasearch engine in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Morocco. Distributes to more than 100 partner platforms.
wego.access: A Wego partner account (manual approval). API key and partner ID once agreed.

TUYA.description: A cloud IoT platform driving millions of white-label devices: locks, cameras, thermostats and sensors. Most low-cost connected objects run on it.
TUYA.access: A project on the Tuya cloud portal (free trial plan): access ID and secret, entered from the card's settings button. Link the Tuya app account to discover the organisation's devices.

MINUT.description: A Swedish sensor built for short-term rentals: it measures noise level without a microphone or recording, plus temperature, humidity and motion. Ideal for preventing parties and disturbances.
MINUT.access: A Minut account and a device (about €150). OAuth2 connection through the dedicated button. Real-time noise alerts included.

BREVO.description: A French emailing platform. Newsletter campaigns, transactional emails and contact management (waiting list, quote requests). A GDPR-compliant alternative.
BREVO.access: A Brevo account (free tier up to 300 emails a day). API key under Settings → SMTP and API → API keys.

whatsapp_business.tooltip: Meta's official WhatsApp Business interface: transactional messages (booking confirmation, check-in…), approved templates, rich media and a catalogue to sell extras in the chat. WhatsApp is the leading channel in Morocco and Saudi Arabia.
whatsapp_business.access: Configure the provider per organisation, directly from Baitly.

airdna.tooltip: The reference platform for short-stay market analysis: average rate, occupancy and revenue by area. Covers Marrakech, Casablanca, Riyadh, Jeddah, Paris and all of France. Useful to decide on an investment or benchmark against local competitors.
airdna.access: Take out a subscription (from about €20 a month per market), then request an enterprise API key for the integration (a sales contact is required).

mytse.tooltip: A French solution that automates calculating, collecting and filing the tourist tax with local councils. Compliant with the current scales, with reporting that matches the mandatory monthly returns.
mytse.access: Free account creation, priced on the volume of nights declared. The API key is issued once the account is approved.

avalara.tooltip: A US tax compliance platform. It automates collecting and remitting tourist tax for short-term rentals. Covers more than 5,000 jurisdictions worldwide, including France, Morocco and the UAE.
avalara.access: An Avalara account is required; the API key is issued once contracted. Priced on the number of active properties.

efacture_dgi_ma.tooltip: The Moroccan tax authority's electronic invoicing system, rolling out gradually. In time, invoices from Moroccan businesses will have to be filed and validated through the platform. Baitly is preparing the connection from its compliant invoicing module.
efacture_dgi_ma.access: A tax ID and company registration on the authority's portal. The API specification will be published as the rollout proceeds: record your credentials now.

superhog.tooltip: A UK guest screening and damage deposit service for short-term rentals. Biometric and ID checks, with a deposit covering up to €5 million. Widely used by premium managers in France and the UK.
superhog.access: A manager account is required (properties are approved), then an API key. Priced per booking (about €3–€8 per stay) or by annual subscription.

safely.tooltip: A US equivalent of Superhog: background checks, damage insurance and liability cover. Relevant for international guests and premium short stays.
safely.access: Online registration and verification of your property portfolio. Priced per stay (about $3–$7). A REST API is provided after onboarding.

axa_partners.tooltip: The AXA group's travel insurance arm: cancellation cover, medical assistance and baggage, offered at booking to raise revenue per stay through a referral commission. Particularly relevant in France and Morocco.
axa_partners.access: A business partnership agreement is required (sales contact). Integration through a REST API and a portal to manage the policies sold.

tawuniya.tooltip: Saudi Arabia's long-established insurer and market leader in travel and damage cover. Offers policies tailored to tourism and short stays.
tawuniya.access: A business partnership (direct contact through the agencies or the corporate portal). API documentation is available once agreed.

turno.tooltip: A North American and European marketplace of cleaners specialised in short-term rentals: automatic scheduling between bookings, photo checklists and built-in payment. Growing in France and Morocco.
turno.access: A free manager account and a free marketplace (commission on the cleaner's payment). A REST API is open to partners (request it through the developer portal).

properly.tooltip: A visual checklist app for cleaning teams: every step is validated with a photo. Enables remote quality control and traceability for damages or condition reports.
properly.access: A per-property subscription (about $5–$10 a month). An integration API is available for partner systems.

breezeway.tooltip: A leading operations platform in the US and UK for short-term rentals: cleaning, maintenance, inspections and team communication. Highly polished, used by large management agencies.
breezeway.access: A pro subscription (about $8–$15 per property per month depending on the plan). Integration API through their partner portal.

igloohome.tooltip: A Singaporean maker of PIN and Bluetooth locks. A 12- to 18-month battery and no need for permanent Wi-Fi, which matters above 45 °C in summer. Codes are generated in advance and expire automatically.
igloohome.access: Buy the hardware (about €200–€400 per lock), open a free developer account, then get an API key for temporary code generation.

ttlock.short: Budget locks · Morocco and Middle East
ttlock.tooltip: A Chinese ecosystem of low-cost Bluetooth locks (about €50–€150 each). Very common in Morocco and in budget rentals. An open API generates time-limited codes.
ttlock.access: A free developer account on the portal (client ID and secret), with the hardware purchased separately.

tuya_smart.tooltip: A cloud platform standardising more than 500,000 connected devices: locks, thermostats, sensors, plugs. Ideal for a mixed estate, since most white-label brands run on it.
tuya_smart.access: A free developer account: create a project to get the access ID and secret. The free quota covers most uses.

ecobee.tooltip: Premium smart thermostats (Canada): remote scheduling, presence detection, energy savings around 23%. Useful to avoid heating or cooling between guests.
ecobee.access: Buy the thermostat (about €250–€300). Free developer registration and an OAuth2 connection to the REST API.

resideo.tooltip: The home automation division spun out of Honeywell: thermostats, water sensors, smoke and carbon-monoxide detectors. Relevant for multi-property agencies wanting one professional solution.
resideo.access: A free developer account and an OAuth2 connection. Hardware bought from the usual distributors.

getyourguide.tooltip: Europe's leading tourist activities platform: more than 200 destinations, monument ticketing and guided experiences. Ideal cross-selling for your guests, with a 15–20% referral commission on each booking.
getyourguide.access: Free registration to the partner programme for a referral ID. An optional API key displays the catalogue natively. No minimum volume.

klook.short: Activities marketplace · Asia and Middle East

viator.tooltip: A TripAdvisor subsidiary with a very broad catalogue of activities and experiences. An 8% referral commission. A strong presence in France, Europe and worldwide.

trustyou.tooltip: A German review aggregation platform: multilingual sentiment analysis (including Arabic), competitive benchmarking and real-time alerts. Affordably priced for management agencies.

hijiffy.tooltip: A Portuguese conversational AI platform for hospitality: a pre-stay assistant (FAQs), in-stay concierge and post-stay automated review requests.

mailchimp.tooltip: A reference email marketing platform for small businesses: drip campaigns, guest segmentation and responsive templates. Free up to 500 contacts, ideal for independent hosts.

klaviyo.tooltip: A premium Mailchimp competitor focused on conversion: deep behavioural segmentation, automation flows and A/B tests. Used by agencies selling stays direct.

dashboardKpis.instruction: Select a metric to see the recommendation

hints.occupancy: Sold nights out of available nights

basis.occupancy: Occupancy in the period, excluding closed, unsold nights.

dashboardKpis.caveat: Indicative Baitly guideposts, not market benchmarks. Seasonality, location, closed dates and portfolio changes can affect interpretation.
dashboardKpis.sampleRule: No rating without a positive baseline; reservations require at least 5 in the previous period. A rising ADR remains on watch when RevPAN falls or cannot be compared.

reasons.noReviews: No usable reviews in this period. Invite guests to share feedback after departure to start measuring satisfaction.
reasons.noData: There is not enough usable data to assess this metric. Check active properties, open nights and data synchronisation.
reasons.noBaseline: No positive, comparable baseline is available. Check imported history; starting from zero does not establish strong growth.
reasons.fewReviews: This rating is based on fewer than 5 reviews. Read the feedback and invite guests to review their stay before drawing a trend.
reasons.fewBookings: The previous period has fewer than 5 reservations. Compare a longer period before interpreting a significant rise or fall.
reasons.priceBalance: Average prices are stable or rising, but revenue per available night does not confirm this trend. Check occupancy and unsold nights before raising rates.

occupancy.excellent: Occupancy is high. Maintain service quality and compare ADR with RevPAN to identify dates where rates could be adjusted.
occupancy.good: Occupancy is solid. Find gaps between stays and review minimum stays to make better use of open nights.
occupancy.watch: Occupancy needs monitoring. Compare properties and channels, then check visibility for available dates.
occupancy.alarming: Many open nights remain unsold. Check channel connections, stay restrictions and rates for approaching dates.
occupancy.critical: Very few open nights are sold. First check listings and synchronisation, then examine each property before adjusting offers.

revenue.excellent: Revenue is growing strongly. Identify the properties and channels driving growth, then check how costs are changing.
revenue.good: Revenue is stable or growing. Compare occupancy with average rates to understand what supports this result.
revenue.watch: Revenue is declining moderately. Compare sold nights and average rates, allowing for seasonality and portfolio changes.
revenue.alarming: Revenue has fallen substantially. Identify affected properties and review the relevant reservations, cancellations and rates.
revenue.critical: Revenue has dropped sharply. First check data quality and connections, then focus on the properties explaining the decline.

adr.excellent: Average rates are rising with stable or higher RevPAN. Check that reservations and guest satisfaction support this change.
adr.good: Average rates are stable or rising. Compare properties to preserve a healthy balance between rates and occupancy.
adr.watch: Average rates are falling. Check discounts and property mix; lower rates can still help if occupancy and RevPAN improve.
adr.alarming: Average rates have fallen substantially. Check stacked promotions, channel rates and unusually cheap stays.
adr.critical: Average rates have dropped sharply. Check pricing errors, currencies and discounts before changing your strategy.

revpan.excellent: Revenue per available night is growing strongly. Separate the effect of rates and occupancy, then repeat effective practices.
revpan.good: Revenue per available night is stable or growing. Compare properties to identify room for improvement.
revpan.watch: Revenue per available night is falling. Look at occupancy and ADR together to find the weakening factor.
revpan.alarming: Revenue per available night has fallen substantially. Prioritise properties with the most unsold nights or steepest rate drops.
revpan.critical: Revenue per available night has dropped sharply. Verify data, calendars and rates, then plan actions for each property.

bookings.excellent: More stays are starting in the period. Plan arrivals and cleaning while monitoring stay length.
bookings.good: Stay volume is stable or growing. Keep availability current and ensure your team can manage the arrivals.
bookings.watch: Fewer stays are starting in the period. Check their length too: fewer reservations do not necessarily mean fewer sold nights.
bookings.alarming: Stay volume has fallen substantially. Compare channels and stay length, then check listing visibility.
bookings.critical: Stay volume has dropped sharply. Check synchronisation and booking restrictions before launching a sales initiative.

rating.excellent: Guests appreciate their stay. Identify recurring strengths and maintain these standards with your team.
rating.good: Feedback is positive. Respond to reviews and address recurring minor issues to improve the experience.
rating.watch: Satisfaction needs monitoring. Group recurring comments and choose a concrete improvement for upcoming stays.
rating.alarming: Satisfaction is low. Address recurring problems promptly and check reported cleaning, arrival and amenity issues.
rating.critical: Satisfaction is severely degraded. Contact affected guests and prioritise resolving issues before new arrivals.
